context: Either have bulk_transfer omit autoincrement PK columns when the caller asks for additive semantics (letting SQLite assign fresh ids), or generalise the offset approach into bulk_transfer so any caller gets it. Prefer whichever keeps row ORDER intact for append-only tables -- finding_events order is its meaning, so a fresh-id path must preserve relative order.
description:
todo_db.bulk_transfer builds its INSERT column list from PRAGMA table_info, which includes the autoincrement primary key, and copies staged values verbatim. Any transfer into a target that already holds rows with those ids fails on the first collision and rolls the whole transfer back.

This is not hypothetical: the phase-5 findings import hit it. Staging numbered finding_events.seq from 1 while production already held seq=1 from an earlier sync, so the very first insert would have aborted the entire 432-row transfer. It was found only by reading the target's maxima before writing -- the scratch-DB rehearsal could not surface it because that database was empty of findings.

The items domain is currently immune by accident, not by design: its only bulk caller uses --replace, which DELETEs every TRANSFER_TABLE first, so ids are always free. Any future additive (non-replace) transfer into a populated target reopens this.

Mitigated for findings only, by todo_findings.offset_staging_pks + target_findings_maxima. The general fix belongs in bulk_transfer.

anti_patterns.dont: Reassign ids in a way that reorders rows
anti_patterns.instead: preserve relative order explicitly and assert it in a test
anti_patterns.why: finding_events and events are append-only audit trails where sequence order carries the meaning

anti_patterns.dont: Test only against an empty target
anti_patterns.instead: cover a target that already holds rows at the same ids the staging database uses
anti_patterns.why: an empty target is exactly the case that hid this bug through a full scratch-Turso rehearsal

preserves.behavior: Append-only table row ORDER survives any id reassignment (finding_events order is the audit trail's meaning)
The existing --replace transfer path stays byte-for-byte equivalent, including copied ids
todo_findings.offset_staging_pks keeps working, or is removed only once bulk_transfer subsumes it

verifications.description: tracker script tests pass, including an additive transfer into a target with colliding ids

work_units.evidence: PR #1540: two tests seed the target with rows at the staged ids before transferring. Both fail on the unfixed tree with 'hosted pipeline error: UNIQUE constraint failed: events.seq' - the empty-target blind spot that hid this originally is closed by seeding first.
work_units.summary: Add a failing test: additive bulk_transfer into a target that already holds rows at the staged ids

work_units.evidence: PR #1540 then corrected by #1544. Additive transfers omit reassignable PKs so SQLite assigns fresh ids in INSERT order; rows selected ORDER BY that key. #1540's first cut sniffed for any rowid alias, which review correctly flagged as unsound - deferrals.id is a rowid alias but is referenced by value from events.detail and from promoted item prose, so reassigning it would silently re-point audit rows. #1544 replaced the sniff with an explicit allowlist (events.seq and the four findings PKs); deferrals is excluded and now aborts loudly.
work_units.summary: Decide and implement PK-safe additive semantics (omit autoincrement PKs, or fold the offset into bulk_transfer)

work_units.evidence: Order: test_additive_transfer_preserves_append_only_order asserts staged event order survives reassignment. offset_staging_pks: reconciled not removed - the findings import calls bulk_transfer additively so it is now subsumed, and its comment claiming 'bulk_transfer copies primary keys verbatim' was corrected in place. Kept because it is independently tested. Residual deferrals gap logged as bulk-transfer-deferral-id-reference-remap.
work_units.summary: Assert append-only row order survives, and reconcile or remove todo_findings.offset_staging_pks
